title: FAFSA Verification Panic Binder
oneLiner: A family-safe aid appeal workspace that shows exactly what documents to gather after a FAFSA mismatch.
targetUser: First-generation students, parents, transfer students, and school counselors dealing with FAFSA verification, family-status mismatches, tax-data errors, or aid holds.
keyUx: Answer a short intake about the flagged mismatch, then receive a document path, office-contact map, deadline clock, and plain-language explanation of what to ask the school financial-aid office.
externalSignals: Signal 6: FAFSA identity-theft/tax mismatch causing revoked aid and tuition hold risk - https://www.reddit.com/r/FAFSA/comments/1s927my/my_dads_identity_was_stolen_and_its_affecting_my/
Signal 7: FAFSA verification panic after parent marital-status mismatch - https://www.reddit.com/r/FAFSA/comments/1t28ksc/i_made_a_mistake/
stitchPrompt: Build a web app prototype called "FAFSA Verification Panic Binder" for first-generation students and families facing aid verification after a FAFSA mismatch. The interface should include a calm intake wizard, mismatch type cards, required document checklist, family timeline builder, school financial-aid office contact script, deadline and hold-risk tracker, and appeal packet export. Use realistic sample data: parent identity theft tax issue, separated parents marked incorrectly, transfer school verification link, and risk of account hold. Design direction: apply the `calm-consumer` profile with reassuring spacing, warm neutral surfaces, plain-language microcopy, and highly visible next-step checklists for anxious families.
